transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-18
Start: 16:15 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonas (Redwood SE), Elliot (TO CTO), Priya (Lead ML Eng), Rafael (Platform Eng)

Summary:
Quick discovery to understand Transparent Onramp's time-to-first-token needs, decide between Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private, clarify free credits/quickstart, and outline a pilot and benchmark plan. Security, data residency, and KMS requirements surfaced. Next steps: pilot plan, benchmark script, and traffic profile.

Topics: quickstart credits, hosting fit, latency vs cost tradeoffs, SOC2/KMS/SAML, time-to-first-token, pilot acceptance criteria

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh i'm maya with redwood inference. Jonas our solutions engineer is with me. How are you all?
[00:07] Elliot: good, thanks. we've got about 45 minutes, trying to move quick. I'm Elliot, CTO. Priya and Rafael are on to talk specifics.
[00:13] Priya: hey, quick note — we're evaluating a couple of routes: quickstart in hosted, or go straight to dedicated for predictable throughput. main constraints are latency under 200ms p95 on chat completions and strict data residency for EMEA.
[00:25] Jonas: got it. quick question on traffic shape — is that 200ms p95 on the 1k token prompt or average shorter prompts?
[00:31] Priya: mostly short prompts, 50–120 tokens, but bursts of 200–400 concurrent requests (we're scaling during end of day).
[00:38] Rafael: and we must keep raw transcripts encrypted and not leave our VPC. that's non-negotiable for the pilot.
[00:44] Maya: cool, that's helpful. On the credits/time-to-first-token side we offer a PLG quickstart — free credits to get to first call, self-serve onboarding, plus we can do a SE-led quickstart if you want help. That usually gets teams to a successful call in 1–2 days.
[00:58] Elliot: i'd like clarity: with the free credits, are we blocked from doing any performance tests? we need real latency numbers.
[01:04] Maya: no, you can run performance tests on hosted for the quickstart, though for the highest throughput and guaranteed p95 you'd look at Dedicated. We can also spin a private pilot (VPC) if data residency/KMS is required.
[01:16] Priya: with hosted, does the KV cache or prefix caching persist between requests? We rely on cached contexts heavily.
[01:21] Jonas: yes, we have prefix/KV caching on the runtime. small caveat — on shared hosted pools cache lifetime is shorter than on dedicated, so if you need warm KV cache persistency we'd recommend dedicated or a VPC private deployment.
[01:34] Rafael: and KMS integration? we use AWS KMS + HSM on some keys.
[01:38] Jonas: supported. we integrate with customer KMS for Private and Dedicated through a keywrap pattern; on hosted we offer envelope encryption but if you need BYOK/HSM you'd go Private. sometimes customers ask for SAML/SSO as well — we support SAML + SCIM for RBAC in enterprise plans.
[01:53] Elliot: okay. timeline: we want a two-week pilot, show we can hit latency and cost targets. can Redwood provide a benchmark script?
[01:59] Maya: yes. Jonas, can you outline the benchmark approach?
[02:02] Jonas: sure. we'll give you a simple harness that replays your traffic profile against a Redwood endpoint, with options for concurrency and varying sequence lengths. we instrument token-level latency and cost, and provide a CSV with p50/p95/p99 and token throughput. takes about a day to wire up if we have sample traffic.
[02:17] Priya: great — we'll share traffic histogram. question on model options: we have a fine-tuned small model in house and later want to host a larger open model. can Redwood serve custom weights?
[02:27] Jonas: we support model variants and pinned versions for serving. Private deployments let you bring your own model binaries; for hosted we can onboard vetted weights via model onboarding process (there's a security review). fine-tuned models often run on Dedicated for throughput.
[02:40] Elliot: training artifacts must not persist. can you confirm audit logs and retention settings?
[02:44] Maya: yes — logs and audit trails are configurable. Private and Dedicated allow customer-managed log sinks. Hosted has standard retention but we can map that out in the security docs. I'll attach SOC2 and the infra architecture doc right after.
[02:57] Rafael: any compliance certifications for hosted? SOC2 Type II is a must.
[03:01] Maya: hosted is SOC2 Type II. We also publish pen test summaries and have an enterprise security pack for HIPAA/ISO discussions.
[03:10] Priya: ok — cost question: can you ballpark token cost for short chat prompts on hosted vs dedicated?
[03:15] Maya: rough back-of-envelope: hosted per-token rate is higher but you pay only for usage; Dedicated reduces unit cost significantly at commit levels. Eg, for a small chat model you might see 2–3x savings on Dedicated at 1M tokens/day sustained. We'll put exact numbers in the pilot pricing.
[03:29] Elliot: are there burst/burst credits? we have unpredictable traffic spikes.
[03:33] Jonas: Dedicated has burst capacity options; you can configure autoscale policies with burst bandwidth. Also smart routing can failover to hosted if dedicated capacity is saturated — that keeps the app up but may affect cost/latency. That's part of an SLO-based routing policy.
[03:49] Priya: we care about cold-start latency for model loads — what are typical cold start times for bigger open models in your runtime?
[03:55] Jonas: depends on model and quantization. For a 13B fp16 model, warm generates normally under 150ms/token; cold starts can be tens of seconds for a full load unless you use pre-warmed pools or batching. We recommend continuous warm pools for production.
[04:10] Elliot: ok, that helps. question from my side — if we start with hosted quickstart and then move to Dedicated mid-pilot, how smooth is the transition? downtime?
[04:18] Maya: we can route traffic to a dedicated endpoint while keeping hosted as fallback. Transition is mostly config and DNS-level cutover; we typically run a canary then cut traffic. No major downtime expected.
[04:27] Rafael: about network: our legal says no egress of raw content from EMEA. private deployment or VPC seems required. what's the shortest path to get a VPC private pilot?
[04:36] Jonas: we can provision a private pilot in a customer VPC region in 2–3 weeks depending on procurement and infra access. If timeline is tight, we can do hosted pilot limited to EU-region endpoints with additional contractual controls while you complete private setup.
[04:51] Priya: for acceptance criteria, we propose: 1) p95 latency <200ms for 50–120 token prompts at 200 concurrent, 2) encryption in transit+at-rest with customer KMS, 3) no PII retention beyond processed output. Do those map to Redwood's monitoring?
[05:04] Jonas: yes — we emit token-level latencies, retention policies are configurable, and we can show evidence for the retention requirement. We'll also add regression alerts tied to prompt sets.
[05:13] Maya: quick commercial note — we can do a 2-week pilot with X credits (we discussed free credits for quickstart), then pricing options for Dedicated pilot. I'll send a tailored pilot scope and expected costs.
[05:24] Elliot: cool. curious — who else integrates with you for vector storage? we currently use Pinecone and Milvus.
[05:30] Maya: we have integrations and recommended patterns; we'll share our integration guide.
[05:35] Priya: last question — will you share a simple checklist for time-to-first-token (TTFT)? we want dev onboarding to be low friction.
[05:42] Jonas: yes — typical TTFT checklist: API key creation, SDK install, minimal client sample, generate-first-call, stream handling, and optionally pre-warm/async batching settings. With our quickstart, teams hit a first successful call in under a day, and a prototype in 1–2 days if they have example prompts.
[05:58] Elliot: sounds good. let's summarize next steps.
[06:01] Maya: recap — Redwood: send pilot plan + pricing + SOC2 and architecture docs, Jonas: benchmark harness and TTFT checklist, Transparent Onramp: share traffic histogram and SLOs. Customer to decide hosted quickstart vs VPC pilot timeline.
[06:14] Priya: yes, we'll aim to send the histogram by monday.
[06:18] Rafael: procurement will need contract terms for private deployment, i'll loop in legal after we see pilot pricing.
[06:24] Maya: perfect. i'll follow up with an email and link to the pilot doc (link: https://redwood.ai/pilot-plan) and security pack (link: https://redwood.ai/security).
[06:33] Elliot: thanks, everyone. end call.
